label: Original-phase input of d/b/e/k/w/m/v/3/s at position >= 3
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase. It never fires at t=0, the <DEL> step, or anywhere in the copy phase. Within the input phase it is token-selective: the input is one of d, b, e, k, w, m, v, 3, s. d is strongest (31% fire rate, 26% of activation mass), then b. The rate climbs with position (orig_idx 1: 0.9%, orig_idx 5-7: about 21%), so it mostly fires late in the input and just before <DEL>. It favors the first occurrence of a token (in_first: 88% of mass). Context modulates it: it fires more when earlier tokens include 0/j/g/i/1/n/2/c and often stays silent when the prefix holds many other letters (q, t, u, x). Adding a seen-context condition raised precision to 0.6 but cost recall, so it was left out. Dev: P=0.50, R=0.80, F1=0.62, mass recall 0.88. Precision is limited because whether it fires on a trigger token depends on the accumulated prefix in a graded way.
